newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude prices steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude prices steady in quiet trade.

text.p: North Sea crude markets were steady in quiet trade on Friday afternoon, with the recent slide in premiums appearing to have bottomed out, traders said.
After rallying to a four-month high of $21 per barrel in early trade, October Brent futures were pegged back to trade around the $20.70 support level over the afternoon.
Physical trade across the North Sea grades was thin after an active trading day on Thursday, and a gas oil-aided improvement in refining margins saw some prompt market length tidied up.
"It was a busy day yesterday and many people have now squared out ahead of the U.S. holiday weekend," a trader said.
Industry functions also helped to dull activity.

Dated Brent was valued around October +25 cents, steady on Thursday's trade of Sep -25 cents and equivalent to its recent low, probably reflecting buyers' reluctance to pay higher values against October. Sept/Oct Brent was slightly steadier at around +52 cents on Friday, having rallied by 10 cents on Thursday.

Dealers said that Thursday's prompt Oseberg trade at Dated Brent +15 cents may not be repeated, as the next offer was at +25 cents. "I think we might have seen the bottom of the differentials. The second half of September looks stronger than the first half," a North Sea producer said.
Mediterranean sour crudes were looking firmer on Friday, bolstered by improved refining margins and the removal of prompt barrels from the market, traders said.
A large cargo of benchmark Russian Urals, originally due to load Sept 1-3 but sold as a Sept 7-10 loader, fetched Dated Brent less $1.03 a barrel cif Med on Thursday.
Late August barrels sold Wednesday at Dated Brent -$1.10.
"Margins are looking a little brighter with gas oil and fuel picking up a bit. It's certainly off the bottom but whether people will come out now and buy is a different matter," said a trader.
Unsold Syrian and Iranian cargoes were denting the positive outlook, traders said.

West African crude markets were mixed with distillate-rich grades holding on to recent gains and lighter barrels easing back. Fresh direction was still dependent on the result of India's October tender, due to be awarded later on Friday, traders said.
A VLCC of Bonny Light and as many as five VLCCs of Qua Iboe were offered into the tender, traders said.
Traders expect India to make a large award to compensate for modest October diesel purchases earlier this week, although only three Dubai cargoes are offered.
